facts.text: In the late 1800s, Wernersville blossomed into a resort town, boasting hotels like Galen Hall, Bynden Wood, Grand View, and the Highland Hotel.
The historic Lerch Tavern on West Penn Avenue now serves as a museum and non‑circulating library dedicated to local history.
The Heidelberg Heritage Society restored the Wernersville Passenger Station, a former Reading Railroad stop, and it still hosts special events.
In 1891, the Wernersville State Hospital opened as the State Asylum for the Chronic Insane, and its original buildings remain active today.
Wernersville sits at 40°19′48″N 76°4′51″W in the foothills of South Mountain, a favorite retreat for city dwellers seeking cool mountain air.
The town once hosted the Jesuit Novitiate and Juniorate of St Isaac Jogues before relocating to Syracuse in 1993.
